## Part 3 — Three Tiers + Build-Your-Own

Renamed in the brand's vocabulary: **Open / Studio / Foundry**, with **MIT Core** as the free base that always exists underneath.

### MIT Core (free, always available — not a tier, the floor)
The current public skill, MIT-licensed, community-supported, GitHub issues only. Stays exactly as is. This is the marketing engine and the credibility anchor.

---

### Tier 1 — **Open+** *(Lite)*
- **Configuration:** MIT license / Core + 1 vertical pack / Community Discord / 1 blueprint review per month / Self-hosted memory / JSON-YAML only / Monthly updates / Opt-in training data
- **Positioning:** For the solo consultant who's using the free skill seriously and wants one expert pair of eyes per month plus their industry's dimension pack.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored at "less than one hour of the consultant's own billable rate per month" (+$A/mo). The review is the load-bearing value — everything else is sweetener.

### Tier 2 — **Studio** *(Core — flagship)*
- **Configuration:** Commercial single-seat or 5-seat / +3 vertical packs / Private Slack 48hr / 3 blueprint reviews/mo + live debug / Hosted single-user memory / +3 platform integrations / Weekly updates + early access / Opt-out training data
- **Positioning:** For the boutique agency or coaching practice running the skill across multiple clients and wanting reliable expert backup plus the configurator wired into their actual stack.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored at ~3–4× Open+. Sum-of-parts via BYO would price meaningfully higher (+$C); flagship is the rational choice for anyone needing more than one review and any real integration.

### Tier 3 — **Foundry** *(Premium)*
- **Configuration:** Private fork / All packs + custom dimension authoring / Dedicated Slack 4hr / Unlimited reviews + live debug / Hosted team-shared memory / Custom integration build / Weekly + early access / Contractual training-data exclusion
- **Positioning:** For consultancies, accelerators, and PE-backed services firms productizing dozens of offerings across a portfolio, where the skill becomes internal IP.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored against the cost of hiring a productization consultant for a single engagement (+$E). Foundry is "infinite engagements for less than two." Below the sum-of-parts of Studio + custom dev work + named expert retainer.

### Build-Your-Own Framework

**Base:** Open+ at +$A/mo.

**Per-dimension upgrades (monthly):**
- Vertical Packs: +1 pack (+$P) · +3 packs (+$3P × 0.7) · All + custom authoring (Private fork required)
- Support Channel: Discord → Private Slack 48hr (+$S) · → Dedicated 4hr (+$3S, multi-seat required)
- Human Review: +1/mo (+$R) · 3/mo + live debug (+$3R × 0.8) · Unlimited (+$8R)
- Memory: Self-hosted → Hosted single (+$M) · → Team-shared (+$3M, multi-seat required)
- Integrations: +1 platform (+$I) · +3 (+$2.5I) · Custom build (Private fork required)
- Update cadence: Weekly + early access (+$U)
- Training-data exclusion: contractual (+$X, multi-seat required)

**Floor:** Open+ base (+$A/mo). Below this, send them to MIT Core (free).
**Ceiling:** Any BYO config that includes Private fork OR contractual training-data exclusion OR custom integration build auto-routes to **Foundry**. Any BYO totaling above ~80% of Foundry's flagship price auto-routes to Foundry.

**Configurator-enforced dependencies:**
- White-label or custom dimensions → Commercial license required
- 4hr SLA, team-shared memory, contractual data exclusion → multi-seat required
- Custom integration → Private fork required
- Private fork → Foundry only (don't sell forks à la carte)

**Flagship-protection rule:**
- BYO sum to reach Studio's configuration must exceed Studio's flagship price by ~20–30%. Specifically: Open+ base + 3 packs + Private Slack + 3 reviews/mo + hosted memory + 3 integrations + weekly updates + opt-out, summed at BYO rates, must price above Studio. Same constraint for Foundry: BYO sum to match Foundry's config must exceed Foundry's flagship by ~30–40%, making Foundry the obvious choice for anyone wanting a fork or custom dev.
